sources.title: peft/examples/eva_finetuning/README.md at main - GitHub
sources.snippet: The abstract from the paper is: Foundation models (FMs) are pre-trained on large-scale datasets and then fine-tuned on a downstream task for a specific application. The most successful and most commonly used fine-tuning method is to update the pre-trained weights via a low-rank adaptation (LoRA).

sources.title: LoRA · Hugging Face
sources.snippet: LoRA represents the weight updates $\mathrm{\Delta }W$ with two smaller matrices (called update matrices) through low-rank decomposition.

sources.title: GitHub - ml-jku/EVA: One Initialization to Rule them All: Fine-tuning ...
sources.snippet: Before fine-tuning with EVA, you need to create an SVD checkpoint. (the argument svd_filepath in train.sh needs to point to an existing SVD checkpoint). To this end set the variables in bash/run_svd_precompute.sh, such as base_path, model_names and dataset_name, accordingly and execute it. This will create a eva_state_dict in the specified directory.
